elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (b) warrants only that services "will conform to the requirements of this Agreement"; no professional/workmanlike standard appears anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: "the Wet Segment and any software delivered with it will conform to its documentation and to the technical specifications and other requirements of the Supply Contract".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Period is "ninety (90) days following the RFPA Date", not 12 months.
Services limb runs "thirty (30) days following their performance", short of 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Remedy sentence says "repair or replace the non-conforming Wet Segment, software or services", but the retained first sentence of 4.9 (not carved out) still provides that PG members "shall not be liable ... if APCN 2 does not perform in accordance with the technical specifications and other requirements of the Supply Contract, or APCN 2 is not integrated or placed into operation" — a contradictory retained sentence that negates liability for the very non-conformance the remedy addresses.

"refund the amounts paid by that Party in respect of the non-conforming item" is drafted, but the uncarved-out no-liability sentence in 4.9 bars any loss/damage claim for non-conformance, leaving the refund remedy internally inconsistent.

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-law warranty is in the rendered language; the rationale points to Paragraph 25 (p0260), whose text was not supplied, and a mutual covenant is in any event not a warranty.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty appears in the inserted text or cited paragraphs.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Express software-to-documentation warranty: "for a period of ninety (90) days following the RFPA Date, the Wet Segment and any software delivered with it will conform to its documentation".

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "for a period of thirty (30) days following their performance, services performed by the PG under this Paragraph 4 will conform to the requirements of this Agreement" — 30 days is met, though scope is confined to Paragraph 4 services and does not reach the Paragraph 10 maintenance services.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Repair/replace language is present but is contradicted by the retained, un-carved-out first sentence of 4.9 excluding all liability for loss or damage where APCN 2 does not perform to Supply Contract specifications or is not integrated/placed into operation.

Refund of "amounts paid by that Party in respect of the non-conforming item" is drafted, but the same retained no-liability sentence in 4.9 remains operative against it; the carve-outs were inserted only into the second sentence and the (i)-(iii) tail.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.

Duplicate element string: same defect — refund remedy contradicted by the retained liability exclusion in the first sentence of 4.9.

reasons: Finding classification (deviation) is correct: the cited clauses contain only a disclaimer ("the PG does not make any representations or warranties" and "nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as such a warranty or guarantee"), which is the walk-away position, so inserting a fallback conformance warranty is the right response.

Fallback is not complete because the two remedy elements are internally inconsistent with retained language. The carve-outs were inserted only before "the Parties recognize and agree that the PG does not make any representations or warranties" and into the (i)-(iii) tail. The first sentence of 4.9 is untouched and still says PG members "shall not be liable to any other Party ... for any loss or damage ... if APCN 2 does not perform in accordance with the technical specifications and other requirements of the Supply Contract, or APCN 2 is not integrated or placed into operation" — precisely the non-conformance the new warranty covers. Repair/replace and refund are forms of liability, so the retained sentence defeats them.

Repair in operative language: open the first sentence of 4.9 with "Except as provided in Paragraph 4.10, the members of the PG shall not be liable ..." (or add "other than in respect of the warranties given in Paragraph 4.10"), so the liability exclusion no longer swallows the new remedy.

Dangling cross-reference: the disclaimer now twice refers to "Paragraph 4.10", but the inserted warranty block is rendered with no paragraph number. Number the insertion expressly as "4.10" so both cross-references resolve.

Scope note (not fatal at the fallback): the services limb is limited to "services performed by the PG under this Paragraph 4", so maintenance/other services (e.g. Paragraph 10) carry no 30-day conformance warranty. Consider "services performed by the PG under this Agreement" if the fallback is to cover all services.

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, no survival tail, expense, damages or procedural extras are added, and the two short carve-outs are necessary to stop the disclaimer swallowing the warranty. Tying conformance to the Supply Contract technical specifications mirrors the disclaimed standard in 4.9 rather than adding an outside requirement. The Customer-elects remedy choice is more favourable than the model's vendor option and is not an extra.

Preferred level is short of the mark on professional/workmanlike performance, 12-month software period, 90-day services period, compliance with laws and no-malicious-code; those are correctly not asserted, and the comment properly frames the proposal as the fallback.
Comment tone and content are compliant: it explains the disclaimer problem, the added periods and remedies, and the carve-out, in two sentences with the [Playbook] prefix.
